name: quality_momentum_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: High-quality companies (high ROE, low debt/equity, consistent earnings) that also exhibit strong intraday momentum are less likely to experience sharp reversals compared to low-quality momentum stocks. The quality filter acts as crash protection — high ROE, low-leverage names attract institutional buying on dips, creating a floor. The inefficiency persists because quality is typically a long-term factor (monthly rebalancing) and intraday traders ignore it. By restricting momentum trades to high-quality names, we reduce tail risk while maintaining trend-following returns.
mechanism: Multiple independent signals confirming the same direction increase the probability that a genuine order flow imbalance exists, not just noise. When momentum, volume, and volatility signals align, it indicates that institutional activity is creating measurable market impact across multiple dimensions simultaneously, increasing the confidence of directional prediction.

exit.signal_exit: EMA(close,9) crosses EMA(close,21) against position direction

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; skip short entries if VIX < 12 (low-vol bullish regime)

weaknesses: Quality filter is static (changes quarterly) — cannot adapt to rapid deterioration in company fundamentals; a company may report bad results tomorrow while still appearing high-quality today
Asymmetric long/short logic (long quality, short junk) creates directional bias — net long in bull markets, which may not be the strategy's intent
EMA(9)/EMA(21) crossover on 1-min bars generates frequent whipsaws; requires momentum confirmation to filter but still produces false signals in choppy markets
prior_art: Novy-Marx (2013) on quality factor; Asness et al. 'Quality Minus Junk'; momentum factor (Jegadeesh-Titman); quality-momentum combination explored in AQR research papers
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
